transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Redwood CSM), Tom Reynolds (Axiom - Head of ML), Sara Gomez (Axiom - CTO), Elijah Park (Axiom - Infra)

Auto-generated summary:
- Axiom is evaluating expanding their Dedicated capacity into eu-west-1 and adding +20% baseline GPUs for peak season; also wants to extend contract for 12 months with committed discount.
- Action: Redwood to provide updated pricing, run region benchmarks, and provide security docs.

Transcript (timestamps every ~30-60s, imperfect transcription typical of meeting transcript):
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check on audio — looks good. This is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our SE and Marcus from customer success.
[00:09] Tom: Yep, all good. Thanks for making time. We've got about 45 minutes — Sara and I wanted to walk through our capacity plans and confirm the renewal terms.
[00:18] Jordan: Great. Top line, we saw your usage spike in November — congrats on rollout — and it looks like you want to add dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 and increase baseline by roughly 20 to 25%?
[00:29] Sara: Correct. We have seasonal loads in Q1, plus new client integrations in EMEA. We want predictable latency for routing in-region. Also curious on fallbacks — if eu-west saturates, how does Redwood route?
[00:41] Priya: Right, so our smart routing can failover to another region or a lower-cost model variant. For Dedicated we can set policy to prioritise latency vs cost. Note — sometimes the transcript shows 'Redwood Dedicate' but it's Dedicated.
[00:55] Elijah: Quick infra Q: For a private VPC peering, is there any extra network egress we should plan? And do you support cross-region KV cache warming?
[01:07] Priya: We do VPC peering. Network egress depends on cloud provider — we'll put estimated numbers in the pricing. KV cache warming: yes, but cross-region cache has higher latency; we usually warm local caches and have fallback strategies.
[01:22] Tom: For the benchmark, we want to simulate 200 concurrent streams with typical payloads — about 1k tokens avg. Can Redwood run that in eu-west-1 so we can baseline latency and p95?
[01:31] Priya: Absolutely. We'll run a 24-hour run with cold and warm cache phases. I'll include detailed metrics — p50/p95/p99, token cost, and tail latency.
[01:40] Jordan: On pricing, we can offer a committed Dedicated discount if you sign up for 12 months and commit baseline GPUs. Also add-on for additional regions is a small premium. We'll send the formal quote.
[01:52] Sara: Do you have SOC 2 and KMS docs we can share with our security team? Audit's next week and they asked for attestation.
[02:01] Marcus: I have the security pack — I'll share the link after the call. Includes SOC 2 Type II summary, KMS/HSM integration notes, SSO (SAML) flow.
[02:09] Tom: Any known vendor lock-in? We're looking at Anthropic / Vertex options, but we want multi-cloud flexibility.
[02:17] Jordan: No lock-in on the API side — same API across hosted, dedicated, and private. Note that some custom kernels and quant paths are optimized per infra so exact perf may vary, but we keep model compatibility.
[02:31] Sara: On SLA — if we need higher priority during peak, what's the process for burst capacity?
[02:36] Priya: We have burst policies; for Dedicated customers we offer reserved burst pools and can also configure autoscaling policies. If you need guaranteed reserve, we can include burst capacity in the quote.
[02:49] Elijah: For our security team, they asked about log retention and audit logs for inference requests — can Redwood store full audit logs for 1 year?
[02:57] Marcus: Yes, with an enterprise add-on we can retain full logs and S3 export. We'll include retention cost in the proposal.
[03:06] Tom: Good. One small thing — in some notes earlier I saw 'KV cash' — that's KV cache, right?
[03:11] Priya: Yes, KV cache. Transcripts sometimes swap words.
[03:16] Jordan: Ok let's walk through a proposed sizing. Based on your Q4 peak and projected Q1 growth, recommended baseline is 30 A100-equivalent GPUs in a Dedicated pool, with a 20% headroom for peaks. Adding eu-west-1 as secondary region with 8 GPUs to start.
[03:34] Sara: That sizing seems reasonable. How quickly can we spin up eu-west-1?
[03:38] Priya: With Dedicated reserved capacity we can provision in 2–3 weeks pending capacity and contract approval; we can do a pilot in 3–5 days using hosted capacity to validate latency.
[03:48] Tom: Pilot using hosted is fine — we'd like to run both hosted and dedicated comparison. Priya, can you run the benchmark on both so we can see cost/latency tradeoffs?
[03:57] Priya: Yep, we'll do hosted in eu-west and then dedicated in the same region and compare.
[04:03] Sara: About contract — do you support monthly invoicing for committed capacity or only annual?
[04:08] Jordan: We support monthly or annual billing for committed contracts; annual gets better discount. We'll put both options in the quote.
[04:14] Elijah: One operational question: routing policies — can we pin certain traffic (client A) to dedicated pool and other traffic to hosted?
[04:22] Priya: Yes, per-route routing is supported — you can pin customer-specific routes to specific pools or model variants.
[04:29] Tom: Great. Anything else on security? Sara: We're good but will need Redwood to confirm KMS key management modes.
[04:37] Marcus: I'll include our key management doc — we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations.
[04:44] Jordan: Cool — next practical steps: we'll send the quote, Priya runs benchmarks, Marcus shares security pack, Elijah shares network diagram. Any blockers?
[04:53] Tom: None from us — timeline: want to finalize contract by end of month if possible.
[04:58] Jordan: Noted. We'll prioritize the quote.
[05:01] Sara: One more Q on fallbacks: if a regional Dedicated pool gets saturated, can we auto-fallback to hosted in another region without manual failover?
[05:12] Priya: Yes, we have automatic fallback rules; you can configure hard or soft failover thresholds. We'll include recommended defaults.
[05:21] Elijah: For the benchmark, can you also measure cost per 1k tokens across scenarios? That's important for finance.
[05:28] Priya: Yes, cost per token and per inference will be in the benchmark report.
[05:33] Jordan: Ok wrapping — recap of next steps and owners. Marcus will email security docs today, Jordan to send pricing by 12/22, Priya to run perf tests by 1/5, Elijah to share network diagrams by 12/24, Tom/Sara to review contract by 12/30.
[05:50] Tom: Sounds good, thanks all.
[05:53] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up over email and Slack.
[05:57] (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: speaker overlaps minimal, occasional mis-words ('Dedicate'/'KV cash') typical of automated transcription. References shared: link to security pack (sent by Marcus), proposed quote (to be sent by Jordan), benchmark spreadsheet (Priya will share post-run).

End of transcript.
